content: This is a simulation of an electrocardiogram whose purpose is to visualize how devices can estimate the heart rate based on R-R intervals.
I created this visualization when I started using a heart rate monitor (HRM) and got curious about the mysterious value that is heart rate variability (HRV).
I do not have a background in medicine or biology, so I found it simpler to devise a naive cardiogram simulation and use it to calculate a few summary statistics.
After looking at a few real and schematic cardiograms, I decided to generate a sequence of "cycles", each having distinguished PQRSTU points with slightly perturbed wave durations and amplitudes.
By recording each R that the simulation produces, we obtain a sequence of "R-R intervals" and can analyze the simulated heart beat using so-called "time-domain measurements".
We use only the intervals recorded in the last few seconds, depending on how we configure the rolling time window.
The target heart rate parameter controls how often new (randomized) cardiogram cycles are produced.

The calculations we show are simple descriptive statistics; they are explained in [a Kubios blog post](${kubiosBlogUrl}) and are further discussed in the paper ["An Overview of Heart Rate Variability Metrics and Norms"](${overviewPaperUrl}) by Shaffer and Ginsberg (DOI: `${overviewPaperDoi}`).
More complicated methods exist for analyzing HRV, however they require a different approach to visualize.
Furthermore, even the methods we have listed are not interchangeable and are used in different cases, most notably with much larger time windows (minutes and hours rather than seconds).
Anyhow, here is a summary of the statistics above (see either the source code or the Kubios blog post for the calculations themselves):
* SDDR is simply the standard deviation of the R-R intervals (with Bessel's correction), used for long-term HRV analysis (>=24h).
* RMSSD is the "root mean square of successive differences", used for short-term analysis (several minutes).
* pNN50 is the percentage of successive interval differences longer than 50msec, used for even shorter-term analysis.
* IQRRR is the inter-quantile range of the R-R intervals. I haven't seen IQR mentioned elsewhere, so it may be useless for HRV analysis.
The simulation's code can be found [on GitHub](${githubPageUrl}).
